text:
cheng: FYI opened PR 8342 — small kv-cache change + allocator tweak. Observed a tail perf bump on longseq microbench. Attaching bench run and artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/bench/8342/ (raw + flamegraphs). can we do a quick pass? hoping to merge today if canary looks good :pray:

elaine: looking now. quick summary of the regression numbers? :eyes:

cheng: p95 increased ~18ms for 64k longseq on rtx-2x, p99 ~42ms up, throughput (same config) down ~6%. memory per-worker +120MB for that longseq config. short sequences unaffected. baseline vs pr: `master vs pr-8342/2026-03-16` artifacts in the link.

ryan: that p99 delta is worrying. is it the kv eviction path or allocator change? any easy repro?

cheng: initial bisect points to the allocator tweak combined with a change in microbatch packing heuristics — not a single line culprit. I ran isolated runs: turning off the allocator change removes the tail bump.

mo: can you paste the exact bench command you used so I can reproduce locally?

cheng: sure — run this in our perf cluster: ```
./bin/bench --model llama-3-small --seq-length 65536 --batch 1 --iters 100 --tag pr-8342 --capture-flame true
```
results are in artifacts folder `runs/2026-03-16-21-07`

bench-bot: artifacts uploaded — bench: pr-8342/2026-03-16 (s3://redwood-artifacts/bench/pr-8342/2026-03-16). Flamegraphs and alloc traces available.

elaine: thanks. quick look at flamegraphs shows extra time in `alloc::slow_path` and some increased syscalls around memory commit. attaching screenshot (uploaded) :camera_flash:

ryan: if alloc is the culprit, we should consider reverting the allocator tweak or gate it behind a flag. Is the change behind a feature flag?

cheng: it's behind `enable_new_alloc` but default true in canary. I can flip it off for canary runs. I also have a smaller patch to reduce the slow-path frequency I'll push as follow-up.

mo: Can someone approve PR for the revert-on-failure plan? We need 2 approvals to merge. I can lgtm the revert if you post it.

cheng: created follow-up PR 8343 that reintroduces the allocator tweak behind a stricter flag + metrics. If canary fails, we auto-fallback to master behavior. link: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/8343

elaine: I'll +1 8343 after I skim the metrics hooks.

ryan: I can review the revert/canary gating now. If it's safe, i'll approve 8343.

cheng: plan for rollout: merge 8342 + 8343 together, schedule canary with `enable_new_alloc=false` first, then enable for 10% traffic once metrics stable for 30m. If tail persists we revert.

mo: sounds good. request: canary run needed — @bench-bot can you schedule a canary with `enable_new_alloc=false` on the same hardware?

bench-bot: scheduled canary job id=cb-9921 on cluster perf-us-east-2, start ETA 5m. Will post results to this thread when done.

elaine: quick note — add a regression test in perf-suite that runs a single longseq iteration so we catch this in the future. I'll make a ticket.

cheng: added perf-suite test ticket #PT-2219.

bench-bot: canary cb-9921 completed. summary: p95 diff vs master = +2ms, p99 = +6ms, throughput -0.8%, mem delta +12MB. Full artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/bench/cb-9921.

ryan: looks a lot better with the flag off. ok to proceed with merge + canary schedule. I'll approve both PRs after a quick code skim. :thumbsup:

elaine: approving as well, adding a note to the PR about follow-up telemetry to ensure no hidden regression.

cheng: thanks all. merging now and will watch telemetry for next 2 hours. ping here if you see anything odd. :rocket:
